text:
elisabeth: Hey team — Zenith just sent an updated supply file; attaching the CSV in the drive link. They changed how they report reserved vs ephemeral (spot) splits, and included a "normalization_factor" column. Need quick consensus on how we map this to our SKU parity matrix and cost model. TL;DR: does their 'normalization' apply per-GPU or per-pool?

mateo: link? can you paste the header quickly so finance can eyeball the keys? :eyes:

elisabeth: Sure — header looks like: ```sku,region,commit_tier,reserved_pct,ephemeral_pct,normalization_factor,eviction_tail_prob,grace_window_days```

jin: if normalization is per-pool we need to adjust our allocation smoothing. per-GPU would be easier for runtime routing. any note from Zenith on how they compute it?

elisabeth: they wrote: "normalization_factor = effective_compute_equiv / raw_gpu_units". no more detail in the sheet.

priya: For marketplace mapping I'd prefer we treat normalization as a multiplier on capacity (i.e., convert their reserved_pct into effective_reserved_units = reserved_pct * normalization_factor). That preserves our current billing logic. Thoughts?

mateo: That works but we need the delta on unit cost after normalization. If normalization reduces effective units, cost per effective_unit goes up — need to recalc committed vs spot blended rate. I can run a quick sensitivity once I have example rows.

logan: Also flag: their eviction_tail_prob is weirdly high in apac-east — 0.18 on some SKUs. If true, we should include a larger preemptive buffer in the reserve-to-ephemeral fallback policy. Otherwise requests will spill to slower models.

elisabeth: Agreed. I asked Zenith for a small sample (5 rows) with raw_gpu_units and the formula applied. Waiting on reply.

jin: Ops question — when we ingest these CSVs, do we store normalization_factor as-is or compute derived_effective_units and store that? ops-bot, how's the current pipeline?

ops-bot: automated-ingest: schema currently supports float fields for normalization_factor. derived_effective_units is not persisted; we compute on the fly in the pricing pipeline. Would you like a new persisted column? :robot_face:

jin: persist please. helps debugging and backfills when formulas change.

priya: For mapping to SKU parity matrix, propose we add two columns: effective_reserved_units and effective_ephemeral_units (both computed). Also add a source_version tag so we can trace vendor CSV schema changes.

mateo: I'll prepare a quick sensitivity run: baseline cost, after-normalization cost, and a blended reserved/ephemeral unit price. ETA 24h. Will call out any SKUs where effective unit price jumps >10%.

elisabeth: Perfect. Also asking Zenith to clarify whether their grace_window_days applies per-eviction event or per-commit-window. That changes how we credit customer SLAs.

logan: one more nit — sample CSV had region codes as full names ("US West") not ISO. Please normalize to region IDs before ingestion. Little things break the forecast.

priya: noted. I'll add a pre-ingest mapping step for regions and commit_tier names.

elisabeth: Thanks everyone. Action items: @mateo run sensitivity, @jin + ops-bot persist derived fields, @priya add mapping step, and I'll follow up with Zenith for formula clarity and sample rows. Will post the sample when I get it. :+1:

mateo: got it, thanks.

ops-bot: automated-ingest: created ticket #INT-8423 to add derived_effective_units persist and region normalization.

elisabeth: filed as well with Zenith contact cc'd. returning to the drive link once sample arrives.
